headline: Ad Spend at Risk: Fragmented GA4 Tracking, Criteo Retargeting Failure, and Non-Standard Event Taxonomy Undermine ROAS
executiveSummary: During the audited session, critical marketing tracking failed across multiple vendors. Retargeting provider Criteo completely timed out (100% loss of retargeting signal for this session), while Google Analytics 4 (GA4) traffic was fragmented across 3 separate property IDs with 28 network request aborts affecting essential product view and cart signals. Additionally, non-standard event naming (such as 'checkout_gokwik' instead of standard 'begin_checkout' and duplicate 'kp_atc' events on Meta) prevents ad platforms from accurately optimizing campaign bidding towards real bottom-of-funnel buyers.

recommendedNextSteps: Audit and consolidate Google Tag Manager setup to stream all web analytics into one single GA4 Measurement ID, removing secondary IDs (G-VDE0ZFZ4LP, G-5RYZDGXEFH).
Fix Criteo script integration error (net::ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT) to restore retargeting pixel functionality.
Update GoKwik payment integration tags in GTM to fire standard 'begin_checkout' instead of custom 'checkout_gokwik'.
Disable duplicate Meta Pixel app events ('kp_atc', 'kp_visitors') to ensure single-source-of-truth conversion reporting in Meta Ads Manager.

issues.title: Criteo Retargeting Pixel Timed Out Completely
issues.detail: Criteo initialization request (https://gum.criteo.com/fpm/init) failed with net::ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT.
issues.businessRisk: High-intent users viewing this product are not being captured into Criteo retargeting pools. Paid traffic driven to this page cannot be re-engaged via display retargeting, leading directly to wasted ad spend and lost recovery sales.
issues.recommendedFix: Audit Criteo script injection in GTM/Shopify app settings to ensure script host is accessible and not blocked by synchronous script dependencies.

issues.title: GA4 Data Fragmentation Across 3 Property IDs with 28 Failed Beacons
issues.detail: GA4 requests fired to 3 separate IDs; 28 network tracking requests failed with net::ERR_ABORTED including view_item for G-3042L5GP9T at 2954ms.
issues.businessRisk: Session data, conversion credit, and behavioral signals are being split across 3 distinct GA4 properties (G-3042L5GP9T, G-VDE0ZFZ4LP, G-5RYZDGXEFH). Critical events like view_item and page_view failed with net::ERR_ABORTED, causing incomplete funnel attribution and under-reporting conversion rates in main reporting dashboards.
issues.recommendedFix: Consolidate GA4 configuration into a single master Measurement ID in GTM. Remove legacy or duplicate GA4 tags to prevent browser network congestion and request cancellations.
issues.affectedMetric: GA4 Conversion Rate, Purchase Funnel Drop-off

issues.title: Non-Standard Checkout Event ('checkout_gokwik') Breaks Standard Funnel Attribution
issues.detail: GA4 event 'checkout_gokwik' observed at t=10421ms instead of standard 'begin_checkout'.
issues.businessRisk: Using custom event names like 'checkout_gokwik' instead of standard GA4 schema prevents Google Analytics from recognizing when users begin the checkout process. Automated smart bidding tools will fail to optimize for checkout initiation steps.
issues.recommendedFix: Map the GoKwik checkout trigger to fire the standard GA4 'begin_checkout' event with appropriate e-commerce items payload.
issues.affectedMetric: Begin Checkout Conversions / Google Smart Bidding Optimization

issues.title: Duplicate Meta Pixel Signals ('kp_atc' alongside 'AddToCart')
issues.detail: Meta Pixel received 'AddToCart' at t=36862ms and 'kp_atc' at t=38578ms for a single user click.
issues.businessRisk: Firing both standard 'AddToCart' and custom 'kp_atc' on the same user action risks double-counting cart additions in Meta Ads Manager if custom conversions are configured improperly, leading to inflated ROAS reporting and distorted ad set optimization.
issues.recommendedFix: Disable redundant third-party Shopify app pixel events in Meta or standardize event parameters while maintaining a single AddToCart signal.
issues.affectedMetric: Meta Cost Per Add To Cart / ROAS Accuracy

checks.label: The page actually loads
checks.question: Does the ad click land somewhere that works?
checks.method: Asserts the navigation response is HTTP 2xx and that the final URL is on the same host as the requested URL (after stripping "www.").
checks.detail: HTTP 200 on the requested origin -- "Buy The Luxe Loafers in Tan for PU Faux Leather Fit Comfort".

checks.label: Your tags are installed and firing
checks.question: Are the pixels really there, and are they running?
checks.method: Matches every request URL against a table of known vendor endpoints, then asserts GA4 and Meta Pixel each produced at least one request.
checks.detail: All required tags fired: Google Analytics 4, Meta (Facebook) Pixel. 8 vendor(s) detected in total.

checks.label: Nothing fires twice
checks.question: Is anything getting counted more than once?
checks.method: SHA-1 fingerprint over vendor + event name + payload, with volatile params (_p, seq, sid, cache-busters, timestamps) removed. Two hits sharing a fingerprint are a genuine double-fire, not two legitimate events.
checks.detail: 62 event(s) fingerprinted; every payload was unique.

checks.label: The data actually arrives
checks.question: Did the tracking reach Google and Meta, or die on the way?
checks.method: Records the HTTP status of each tracking request and flags any 4xx/5xx or transport-level failure (timeout, aborted, DNS).
checks.detail: High: Criteo request failed · High: Google Analytics 4 request failed

checks.label: One account per platform
checks.question: Is your data being split across duplicate accounts?
checks.method: Extracts the account identifier (tid / id / sid) from every hit and asserts each vendor resolves to exactly one distinct ID.
checks.detail: Medium: Google Tag Manager is reporting to 5 different IDs · Medium: Criteo is reporting to 2 different IDs · Medium: Google Analytics 4 is reporting to 3 different IDs

checks.label: Add to cart gets tracked
checks.question: When someone shows they want to buy, do the ad platforms hear about it?
checks.method: Tags every request with the interaction phase it fired in, then asserts that a conversion-intent event reached each installed ad platform during the add_to_cart phase.
checks.detail: Add-to-cart click produced 2 conversion event(s): Google Analytics 4/add_to_cart, Meta (Facebook) Pixel/AddToCart.

checks.label: Event names make sense to the platforms
checks.question: Can Google and Meta understand what you're sending them?
checks.method: Set membership against the 18 Meta standard events and the 23 GA4 recommended events held in trackingTaxonomy.js. Anything outside them is a custom name.
checks.detail: Medium: 9 non-standard event name(s) in use

checks.label: Nothing dead is still running
checks.question: Are you still sending data to something that shut down?
checks.method: Flags hits to the Universal Analytics collect endpoint, which no longer processes data.
